title: The append path into the central decision ledger is not a published operation
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api: GET /decision-log, GET /decision-log/{entryId} only); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 14 and slide 28
section: Template and Rules v1 §R5.5, DP-03; §R7.2 s12.1
description: The ledger must be written by every service's record, but the Ownership Map gives P7 only the two GET paths and Architecture v5 slide 14 lists no POST for the ledger; the only write is the ingest of rwb.decision-record.v1. The APP story therefore declares no REST write path, and a sibling P7 story (E2028) declares POST /decision-log, which the map does not own.
evidence: ownership.json api rows for P7: GET /cases/{caseId}/recommendation, GET /approvals, POST /approvals/{id}/approve|return|refuse, GET /decision-log, GET /decision-log/{entryId}; no POST on the ledger. Architecture v5 slide 14 rwb-decision IN: GET /decisions?caseId=, POST /approvals/{id}/decide, POST /rule-models.
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-decision service owner
proposed: Confirm the ingest of rwb.decision-record.v1 as the only writer of decision_log_entry, declare no append operation, and align the sibling P7 story that declares POST /decision-log; if a write path is wanted for a service identity, add it to the Ownership Map first and to RWB-P7-E1008-CON.

title: How nineteen local record chains become one central chain is not specified
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 008 (BR3, BR4); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slide 16; Architecture v5 Text Extract slide 28
section: s7 AC2, AC5; s13 chain writer
description: Each of the 19 services writes its own record hash-linked to its own previous record, and the ledger keeps chain_seq, prev_hash and entry_hash as one chain. No source says in which order the records of 19 independent local chains become one central chain_seq, whether entry_hash is recomputed on the ledger's own canonical form or carried from the local record, or how a per-case order is preserved when two services publish at the same moment.
evidence: Temporal and Drools design slide 16: decision record written by the owning service, append-only and hash-chained, JOB-14 checks the chain at 02:00. Architecture v5 slide 28: rwb-decision consumes rwb.decision-record.v1 into the central ledger with chain verification. No ordering or canonical-form rule for the central chain appears in any read source.
owner_role: Solution architect with the decision-center product owner
proposed: Fix the rule as: the ledger recomputes entry_hash on the legacy canonical form (BR4) over the stored columns, orders by the ingest commit under the chain lock, and preserves the local chain sequence and hash on the row for reconciliation; then publish it in RWB-P7-E1008-CON.

title: JOB-13 and FEAT-DRI-06 still describe a data-lake copy that the architecture removes
source: FSD P7 A2.6 (FEAT-DRI-06 Stream the decision log to the data lake, JOB-13 01:00, INT-19); Architecture v5 Text Extract slide 44 (JOB-13 ingest is continuous Kafka) and slide 37; Template and Rules §R6 (RWB-E1-014 retired)
description: The legacy key splits into a ledger with no copy (DP-17, ADR-018) while the FSD module still defines FEAT-DRI-06 with partitions, manifest, watermark and retention of lake partitions, and keeps the id JOB-13 for a 01:00 copy. Architecture v5 reuses JOB-13 for the continuous Kafka ingest and retires RWB-E1-014. Two meanings of one job id and one live feature description remain.
evidence: FSD P7 v3 A2.6 with AC-P7-006-01 (partition business_date, manifest 12,480, watermark) and T5.1 INT-19/INT-20; Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-13 Decision log copy 01:00 -> ingest is continuous (Kafka); slide 37 and DP-17 remove the lake; Template and Rules §R6 retires RWB-E1-014.
owner_role: Business analyst P7 with the enterprise architect
proposed: Withdraw FEAT-DRI-06 and its lake acceptance criteria in the next FSD version, keep JOB-13 as the continuous ingest and JOB-14 as the 02:00 chain check with the WORM seal, and record the retirement of RWB-E1-014 as delivered by the ledger.

title: The strict-mode confirmation a call waits on is not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract slide 28 and slide 44 notes; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (strict mode at points of no return)
description: Four irreversible steps wait for the central ledger to confirm a decision record before executing. No source says what carries the confirmation: a synchronous read of the ledger entry, a reply event on the service topic, or a Temporal signal. The APP story publishes the sealed entry on the shared topic and reads the entry back, and records the ambiguity.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 28: strict decision-log mode applies at each pivot, the step waits for the central ledger acknowledgement before executing. Temporal and Drools design: debt transfer, write-off posting, auction sale and title transfer wait until the ledger confirms the record. No confirmation mechanism is named.
owner_role: Solution architect with the integration lead
proposed: Adopt the read GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId} returning 200 once the entry is sealed as the confirmation, plus the sealed-entry announcement on rwb.decision-record.v1 for the reporting projection, and publish both in RWB-P7-E1008-CON and the integration harness of wave 1.

title: The ledger consumes the shared topic and dedupes in an inbox while its patterns and H row carry no DP-09
source: 04 User stories.../B-P7-01.md story line RWB-P7-E1008-APP (patterns, H); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-09; Architecture v5 Text Extract slides 11 and 20
description: The ledger is a consumer of rwb.decision-record.v1 and dedupes by ce_id in processed_event, which is the outbox and inbox library of DP-09 (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), and it writes an outbox row for the sealed announcement. The WP gives this story DP01, DP03, DP07, DP10, DP13, DP15, DP17, DP19 and no RWB-PLT-TE006-CON in the H row, so DP-09 is unclaimed while its objects are used.
evidence: WP line RWB-P7-E1008-APP: patterns without DP09, H without RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; Architecture v5 slide 11 (inbox processed_event in each consumer) and slide 20 (own schema with outbox and inbox); Ownership Map rows outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key owner PLT.
owner_role: Platform event owner with the rwb-decision tech lead
proposed: Either add DP09 and RWB-PLT-TE006-CON to the H row of the story, or state that the library objects are created by RWB-P7-E1008-DB under the X row and the consumer is built against the published template; the second is the working read of this run.

title: The paging defaults, the maximum page size and the full error body of the decision-log reads are unpublished
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 008 section 12 (page and size named, values absent); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api rows; API Specification v4
description: The legacy contract says the page read has page and size and four error codes, and no source gives the default page, the maximum size, the total field or the body of a problem response beyond the RFC 9457 members. The contract story publishes page 1, size 50, maximum 200 and the five problem members as the working read.
evidence: RWB-E1-008 section 12: 'page and size; response DecisionLogPage; errors 401, 403, 503'. No value for either parameter and no problem body appears in the API Specification v4 entry for the decision-log paths or in the TSD.
proposed: Confirm page 1, size 50 and maximum 200 with an RFC 9457 body carrying type, title, status, detail and the message identifier, and carry the values into RWB-P7-E2005-CON when the filters are added.

title: The ledger read is /decisions on the architecture slide and /decision-log in the Ownership Map
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 14 and slide 41 (first API path /decisions); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api rows GET /decision-log, GET /decision-log/{entryId}
section: s12.1 of RWB-P7-E1008-CON, s12.1 of RWB-P7-E1008-APP
description: Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-decision the read GET /decisions?caseId= and slide 41 the first path /decisions, while the Ownership Map and the API Specification name decision-log. The contract publishes /decision-log under the source precedence of Template and Rules §R3 and records the difference.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 IN: REST GET /decisions?caseId=; slide 41 row P7: First API path /decisions. Ownership Map: GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} with the API Specification v4 basis.
owner_role: Solution architect with the contract owner of rwb-decision
proposed: Keep /decision-log as the published path (legacy name, Ownership Map and API Specification agree) and correct slide 14 and slide 41 in the next architecture version.

title: decision_log_entry.case_id loses the foreign key that the legacy schema and the TSD declare
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql (fk_decision_log_entry_case_id to recovery_case); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2.md T3.3; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-01
description: The legacy table carries a foreign key to recovery_case, and TSD P7 T3.3 declares the relationship, but in the target recovery_case is P3's row in rwb_case and a key would cross a schema boundary that DP-01 forbids and the boundary test fails. The DB story creates case_id as a plain uuid with no key and verifies the case over P3's contract.
evidence: Physical Schema v6: ALTER TABLE decision_log_entry ADD CONSTRAINT fk_decision_log_entry_case_id FOREIGN KEY (case_id) REFERENCES recovery_case (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT. TSD P7 T3.3: decision_log_entry -> recovery_case (Many to 0 or 1). Architecture v5 slide 29 and DP-01 forbid a cross-schema key.
proposed: Drop the key and keep case_id as an identifier verified on the read through the case contract of P3; record the same ruling for every legacy cross-module key of the decision log in the Physical Schema v7 folder.

title: The rwb-decision login, the schema owner separation and the library-object column set are unspecified
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 008 AC1 and section 3 (service role and schema owner role); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json rows outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key
section: s3, s7 AC1, s13 of RWB-P7-E1008-DB
description: The append-only guarantee needs the service login to lack UPDATE and DELETE and the schema owner to be refused by the trigger, but no source names the login, the owner role, the migration account or the column set of the three library objects the DB story creates. The story applies the event platform template unchanged and cites the login by role only.
evidence: RWB-E1-008 AC1 refers to 'the ACE service's database role' and 'the schema owner role' without names; section 3 says the role holds INSERT and SELECT and no UPDATE or DELETE grant. Ownership Map gives no column set for the three PLT library objects.
owner_role: ACE database administrator with the platform DB owner
proposed: Publish the login naming convention of the platform DB work (rwb-<short>_app plus an owner role), keep the migration account separate from the runtime login, and name the template version of the three library objects in RWB-PLT-TE006-CON.

title: The consumer group, the alert thresholds, the verification job time and the seal target of the ledger are unset
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract slides 28 and 44 (5-minute completeness, JOB-14 02:00, daily WORM seal); Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification (no threshold)
description: The deployment must configure a consumer group, a lag threshold, a dead-letter alert, the time of the append-only verification job and an immutable-storage target for the daily seal. The architecture fixes the 5-minute completeness target and the 02:00 run; no source fixes the other values.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 28: within 5 minutes, gap alerts. Slide 44: JOB-14 Hash-chain check 02:00 rwb-decision Schedule. Slide 14 OUT: FILE Immutable storage: daily ledger seal (WORM). No group name, threshold or path appears in any read source.
owner_role: DevOps lead with the platform observability owner
proposed: Adopt group rwb-decision-ledger, one alert at 5 minutes of lag and one at the first dead letter, the verification job one hour before the 02:00 chain check, and a per-environment WORM path agreed with the storage owner.

title: No RPO, RTO or restore-verification standard exists for an append-only ledger
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3 (no backup objective for the decision log); RWB E1 008 BR7 and DL26 (retention only)
description: The ledger may not be repaired by a statement after a restore, so a restore must be proved by the chain and by the WORM seals before promotion. No source gives a recovery point objective, a recovery time objective, the retention of a restore exercise or the point in time a restore may target. The deployment story states the rule and leaves the numbers open.
evidence: The read sources state the append-only rule (REQ-DRI-002) and the retention schedule (DL26) but no backup objective, no restore procedure and no post-restore verification step for the ledger.
owner_role: DevOps lead with the resilience owner
proposed: Set an RPO of zero for committed entries by relying on the PITR of the ACE database plus the seal files, an RTO agreed with the service owner, and make the chain re-verification and the append-only check mandatory gates of every restore.

title: The decision-record write operation is absent from the Ownership Map
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 14, 20, 28 and 41
description: The Ownership Map gives P7 only GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} under /api/recovery/decision/v1 and no write path, while the legacy story's only write surface was a published in-process interface. The story therefore declares no REST append, describes the write as the local decision-record library plus the service-local append, and states that the owned write operation is missing.
evidence: Ownership Map api rows: GET /decision-log (owner P7), GET /decision-log/{entryId} (owner P7); no POST/PUT row for decision-log. Architecture v5 slide 14 rwb-decision IN: REST GET /decisions?caseId= and POST /approvals/{id}/decide only; slide 20 every service writes decision_record in its own schema and publishes DecisionRecorded.
proposed: Keep the append in process under DP-03 and record it in the Ownership Map as a local operation on task queue rwb-decision, or add one owned command path if an out-of-process caller is required; do not add a private path.

title: The full record shape, the data-date column, the inputs digest and the message catalogue entry format are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 027 Decision log writer v1 v1.md sections 11, 12, 14; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031)
section: 11 Data; 12.7 Tables owned; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy story names the field groups and the identifiers DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-030 and DF-DEC-031 but not the column set, the column widths, a data-date column, the inputs digest algorithm, the retention of a local record or the published catalogue entry format of MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P7-003. The stories publish the working read and carry the placeholder.
evidence: RWB-E1-027 section 11 lists the field identifiers only; section 12 lists the Java record fields; section 14 gives the texts and states that Thai follows DL10, with no catalogue entry format; LDM v8 has no data-date column for decision_log_entry.
proposed: Fix the physical column list, the data-date column and the inputs digest in the Physical Schema v6 file rwb_decision.sql and in the contract baseline, and publish the catalogue entry format with the platform message catalogue.

title: The canonical form of the entry hash is not specified
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P7 Decision center and log v3.md A2.1 AC-ALT-P7-001-01; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slide 16
description: The module specification fixes SHA-256 over the canonical form of the entry and the first previous hash as 64 zeros, and the design names prev_hash and entry_hash, but no source fixes the field order, null handling, encoding, separators or digest rendering of that canonical form. Two writers could compute different digests for the same record and the nightly chain check would then report a false break.
evidence: FSD P7 A2.1 AC-ALT-P7-001-01: every entry_hash equals the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form, first prev_hash 64 zeros. Temporal and Drools Design slide 16 lists the record fields and prev_hash/entry_hash with no canonicalisation rule.
proposed: Freeze the canonical form in the contract baseline (ordered field list, UTF-8, no whitespace, null rendered as an empty string, 64 lowercase hex) and publish one cross-language fixture that the store verifier and every writer must reproduce.

title: Two ce_type values are published for DecisionRecorded
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-PLT-LIB Shared libraries/RWB PLT E1027 CON Decision log writer v1 - contract v1.md section 12.3; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P6 rwb-comms (Communications)/RWB P6 E1052 CON Notice generation v1 - contract v1.md AC6 and 12.3
description: The platform library contract publishes the shared event as rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1, while the rwb-comms contract of this run publishes rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on the same shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1. The shared topic name is fixed in both; the type is not, so a registry subject and a consumer binding would differ between services.
evidence: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON 12.3 ce_type rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1; RWB-P6-E1052-CON AC6 and 12.3 rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1; Architecture v5 slide 42 event 08 DecisionRecorded, producer all 19, topic rwb.decision-record.v1.
proposed: Adopt rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 as the single type on the shared topic because it matches the run convention and the rwb-comms contract, correct the platform library contract in its next version, and register the subject once.

title: The decision-log stream to the data lake is retired but still specified

proposed: Delete A2.6 and its acceptance criteria from the next version of the P7 module specification and move the reporting need to the rwb-reporting projection from events.

title: JOB-13 is a 01:00 copy job in the specifications and a continuous ingest in the target
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P7 Decision center and log v3.md A2.6; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 44
description: The module specification runs the decision-log copy as a nightly job at 01:00 with a rerun guard and a retention step, and the legacy scheduling of this service is Quartz-based. The architecture makes the ledger ingest continuous from Kafka and keeps only the 02:00 chain check as a Temporal Schedule, and retires the shared Quartz tables. The writer declares no Schedule.
evidence: FSD P7 A2.6 AC-P7-006-01 and AC-ALT-P7-006-02 (JOB-13 at 01:00, 409 on a concurrent rerun); Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-13 rwb-decision ingest is continuous (Kafka), JOB-14 hash-chain check 02:00 Schedule, no shared Quartz tables; DP-10; Template and Rules §R6 Retired row RWB-TE-007.
proposed: Keep the ingest continuous in RWB-P7-E1008-APP, keep JOB-14 as the only P7 Schedule, and mark JOB-13 as retired in the Batch and Scheduling next version.

title: Decision log retention period is not set

Neither the legacy story nor FSD P7 v3 or TSD P7 v2 fixes a number, a record class or an archive rule for decision_log_entry, and DP-17 removes the lake copy that used to hold the long-term duplicate, so the target has one table and no retention value.
evidence: NFR-030 'The decision log is retained for the period the regulator and internal audit require. Log retention is set by Compliance ... Open, DL26'; Decision Log v10 DL26 'How long is each data product and document type kept ... Provide per data product and document type'; no retention value in FSD P7 A2.1 or TSD P7 T3.1
owner_role: Compliance and PDPA officer, with the P7 business lead
proposed: Compliance fixes the retention period and the archive rule for decision_log_entry as reference data before the wave 2 exit; until then the store keeps every entry, the query purges nothing and archives nothing, and the value is read as a parameter when it arrives.

title: Audit export: a synchronous full-result CSV against a 2 s one-hop budget
source: RWB-E2-005 sections 4 step 7, 12 and AC8; Architecture v5 slide 11 (one hop, 2 s); RWB-P7-E2005-CON section 12.1
section: APP 4 Flow step 11; APP 12.1; CON 11 Data; CON 12.1
description: The legacy flow returns 'the full result as CSV' for a query that AC2 shows matching 200 and the story measures at 10,000 entries, while the target fixes one hop, a 2 s timeout and a page size of at most 500. No source fixes the size of an export, its column order, its file name, or whether the export is one response, a streamed range or a file handed to rwb-integration.
evidence: RWB-E2-005 section 4 step 7 'the Workbench returns the full result as CSV'; section 12 'Accept text/csv for export (additions file)'; AC8 'a CSV file with a header row and 200 entry rows'; Architecture v5 slide 11 'Timeout, retry: 2 s; retry GET only'; TSD P7 T-A.2 API-P7-006 lists no export media type
owner_role: Solution architect, with the TechX lead of rwb-decision
proposed: Keep text/csv on the same GET as the legacy contract allows, stream it page by page inside the service, and read the 2 s budget as per page of 500 rows rather than for the whole population; the export size cap, the column order and the file name are published as the working read until the architect rules.

title: Whether the audit role may see unmasked person keys in an entry or an export
source: RWB-E2-005 section 17 and AC8; NFR-039 and NFR-040; RWB-P4-E1037-CON masking policies
section: APP 11 Data; APP 12.1; CON 11 Data; CON 17 Guardrails

The target makes the masking policy data of rwb-access and gives no unmasking right to RW-AUDIT, but no source states whether the auditor sees the masked or the clear value, or whether the export carries the same masking as the screen.
evidence: RWB-E2-005 section 17 'personal fields in recommendation or actions are masked per the masking rules before export'; AC10 table of section 10 gives RW-AUDIT scope ALL; NFR-039 'Party identifiers are masked at rest ... and on every screen ... by role'; Ownership Map row masking_rule owner P4; FSD P4 masking policy is data with no audit exception named
owner_role: Compliance and PDPA officer, with the P4 access owner
proposed: The audit read and the export carry the masked value under the policy of rwb-access in force, with no unmasking operation on either read; Compliance either confirms that reading or publishes an audit-specific policy row before the wave 2 exit.

title: REQ-ACA-006 and NFR-042 still name a data-lake copy that DP-17 removes
source: Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-ACA-006; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-042; Architecture v5 slide 37 and ADR-018; RWB-E2-005 section 19
section: APP 2 Business rationale; APP 8 BR14; APP 19 Out of scope; CON 2 Business rationale; CON 12.3

Architecture v5 removes the data lake, RWB-E1-014 is retired under the preservation rule and the reporting read model takes the events, so the ledger has no lake copy to log, analyse or reconcile and the two requirement texts name a sink that no longer exists.
evidence: REQ-ACA-006 'Every read of the case store, the document store and the data lake copy is written to the access log'; NFR-042 same wording; Architecture v5 slide 37 (no data lake); Template and Rules §R6 verdict Retired for RWB-E1-014; plan DP-17
proposed: Read REQ-ACA-006 and NFR-042 as covering the case store, the document store and the reporting read model; drop the lake wording at the next BRD and NFR version, retire the lake analysis with no target path and no dependency, and write the AC-READ/AC-EXPT record for the query path only.

title: Scope predicate and Compliance incident queue of the audit read have no owner document
source: RWB-E2-005 sections 4 steps 3 and 5, 10 and 12; Architecture v5 slide 13 note (permission data cached from rwb-access); Ownership Map api and tables
section: APP 3 Preconditions; APP 4 Flow steps 2 and 5; APP 12.2; APP 13 Configuration; CON 12.2
description: The legacy story filters scope through two published interfaces at once — ScopeService.scopeFor of P4 and a P3 interface casesInScope(ScopeFilter, Collection<UUID>) — and names no operation of the Ownership Map for either. In the target the right and the scope are rwb-access's and the case owner is rwb-case's, so a single read has to carry the scope predicate while the case facts stay with their owner. The Compliance incident queue of a chain mismatch is named by no source either.
evidence: RWB-E2-005 section 12 'Published interface used: ScopeService.scopeFor (P4, RWB-E1-037); the P3 interface Set<UUID> casesInScope(ScopeFilter filter, Collection<UUID> caseIds)'; section 4 step 5; Architecture v5 slide 13 notes 'permission data cached from rwb-access'; Ownership Map has no scope operation and no incident-queue row
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P4 access owner and the P3 case owner
proposed: The authorise answer of rwb-access carries the scope kind and the case-scope predicate, the service applies it to the case ID of each entry inside the query, and the case facts of the scope test come from the P3 case read already in the contract dependencies; the incident goes to the Compliance queue read from platform configuration. Confirm both with the two owners.

source: RWB-E2-005 section 13 (V_E2_005__declog_approver_index.sql); RWB-P7-E1008-APP and RWB-P7-E1008-DB; Template and Rules DP-15

owner_role: ACE team, with the TechX lead of rwb-decision
proposed: RWB-P7-E1008-APP owns the table baseline, its keys and its append-only trigger; this story adds one index-only migration, V2005_1__declog_approver_index.sql, in the same rwb-decision sequence after that baseline, and no file of E1008 is edited.

title: First-page performance target over 10,000 entries is assumed and not fixed
source: RWB-E2-005 sections 2 and 13; TSD P7 v2 Appendix T-B (DL11); NFR-036
section: APP 2 Business rationale; APP 13 Build steps; CON 8 BR12
description: The legacy story states the measure as 'the first page of a query over 10,000 matching entries in 3 seconds or less (assumed; DL11)' and marks it negotiable. owner_role: Solution architect, with the QA lead
proposed: Carry 3 s for the first page of 500 rows over 10,000 matching entries as a parameter and test against it in SIT; confirm or replace the number under DL11 before the wave 2 exit.

title: Element list of the audit answer beyond the legacy names, and the element that carries the warning
source: RWB-E2-005 sections 12 and 14; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 API-P7-006 and API-P7-007
section: CON 3 Preconditions; CON 5 X8; CON 11 Data; CON 12.1
description: The legacy contract names items, page, size, total, chainVerified and 'warning MSG-P7-012', and the TSD names only DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry. No source fixes the element names of the eleven audit elements, the element that carries the warning, whether the warning is one string or a list of message codes, the CSV column order or the page-size default, so the contract publishes a working read.
evidence: RWB-E2-005 section 12 'Response: DecisionLogPage: items (DecisionLogEntry plus chainVerified, added in this story), page, size, total; warning MSG-P7-012 when any entry fails'; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 API-P7-006 'Response DecisionLogPage' with no schema
owner_role: Solution architect, with the TechX lead of rwb-decision
proposed: Publish messageCodes on the page, chainVerified on every entry and the eleven audit elements of AC2; the remaining element names, the CSV column order and the page-size default are the working read of ASM-B-P7-01-E2005-8 until the architect freezes them at v1.

title: Message identifier of the 401 answer is not given by any source
source: RWB-E2-005 section 12 Errors; platform message catalogue; RWB-P4-E1037-CON
section: CON 7 AC6; CON 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy contract lists '401' with no message identifier for either read, while every other condition of the same contract carries one. The platform catalogue of the authorise contract names MSG-P4-001 for a token with no Workbench role, but no source read here binds that identifier to the audit read, so the mapping has one row without a value.
evidence: RWB-E2-005 section 12 'Errors: 401; 403 no Decision log R (MSG-P4-002); 422 ...; 503 ...'; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 API-P7-006 'Errors 401, 403, 503' with no identifier; no message catalogue row for the audit read
owner_role: Solution architect, with the platform library owner
proposed: Answer 401 with the platform MSG-P4-001 of the authorise contract once the platform catalogue binds it to these reads; until then the placeholder stands and the contract test asserts the status only.

title: Access record of a query: local decision record or the rwb-access access log
source: RWB-E2-005 sections 4 step 6, 11 and 17; Architecture v5 slides 14, 20 and 28; RWB-P4-E1039-CON; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON AC2
section: APP 8 BR11; APP 12.3; CON 7 AC5; CON 12.3
description: The legacy story writes the AC-READ and AC-EXPT access events as decision_log_entry rows through the writer of RWB-E1-039, which is the access log into the decision log. In the target the access log is P4's (RWB-P4-E1039-CON) and the decision record is local to each service on the shared topic (DP-03, and the access-event exception of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON AC2), so two owners can both claim the record and no source says which one carries it.
evidence: RWB-E2-005 section 4 step 6 'writes one AC-READ access event'; section 11 'Write (AC-READ and AC-EXPT access events through the writer)'; section 3 preconditions list RWB-E1-039; Architecture v5 slide 20 'Own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record'; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON AC2 'an access event carries no case and requires no subject group'
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P4 access owner
proposed: The record is written locally through the decision-record library and relayed on rwb.decision-record.v1, which the P4 access log then reads for its view; P4 keeps the access-log read, the break-glass path and the role model, and no read path of this service calls P4 to write.

title: The delegation of authority table is P4 rwb-access's while the routing rules and the approval resource are P7 rwb-decision
source: Ownership Map v1 (delegation_limit owner P4 and its ruling); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (P4 owns the DoA table) and slide 14; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 and T3.3; legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 4, 8, 11 and 12
description: The legacy story reads the level, the holder and the substitute through the P4 DelegationOfAuthority interface and writes delegation_limit_id and limit_version on the approval. The target keeps the table in rwb_access (P4) and the approval, the routing and the version stamp in rwb_decision (P7), and no source says whether the routing rule itself - the lowest covering level, the no-holder rule and the one-level-up escalation - is P7 code over a P4 read or a P4 rule evaluated for P7. The story keeps the rule in P7, reads the table on the P4 contract and stores a reference, a level and a version only, which is why the same key carries DP-08 and RWB-P4-E1037-CON.
evidence: Ownership Map v1: delegation_limit owner P4, ruling "The DoA table is P4 rwb-access (Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 v3)"; TSD P7 v2 T3.3: "approval | delegation_limit_id | delegation_limit | Many to 0 or 1"; legacy RWB-E2-013 section 11: "DF-REF-018 delegation_limit approval_level Read through the P4 DelegationOfAuthority interface".
proposed: Keep the table, its versions and its holders in rwb-access and give the routing rule to rwb-decision over that read; state in RWB-P4-E1037-CON and in RWB-P7-E2013-CON that the level lookup is a read with a 2 s budget and that the approval stores delegation_limit_id, approval_level and limit_version only, with no join, view or foreign key into rwb_access.

title: The delegation limits operation has no row in the Ownership Map API catalogue
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (rwb-access IN: GET /doa-limits) and slide 41; Ownership Map v1 api section; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 appendix T-A
description: Two architecture slides name GET /doa-limits as a P4 operation, and the P4 row of the service catalogue gives rwb-access the DoA table, but the Ownership Map v1 API catalogue has no GET /doa-limits row at all: the P4 entries it lists are the role, access-log, session, break-glass, list reference and feature paths. The split plan therefore declares RWB-P4-E1037-CON without naming the path, and neither the app story nor its fake can name the operation it reads or the drift test can compare against.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14: "REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) - GET /me/permissions - GET /doa-limits - /masking-policies"; arch v5 slide 41 P4 OUT: "REST Access: DoA limits"; Ownership Map v1 api: no "GET /doa-limits" key among the P4 operations.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-013 (section 11 DF-REF-018, DF-REF-023, DF-REF-024; section 12 consumed P4 interface)
proposed: Add GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits to the Ownership Map catalogue with P4 as owner and to the operation list of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, with the query (decision, regulation item, product, amounts, on-date) and the answer (delegation row reference, level, holder, substitute, version, effective date); until then the story and the baseline use that path and one fake derived from it.

title: The escalation ceiling and the service level values of an approval are not specified
source: legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 3, 4 step 9 and AC2 and AC3; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (escalation_level) and T3.2 (LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-30 and R-UNI-42; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44
description: The routing runs on values the legacy story itself marks as assumed: rwb.approval.route.D7.1.service-level = 1 working day and rwb.approval.service-level.default = 3 working days (DL22), and each escalation gives a new due time one working day later. No source gives the number of escalation levels, what happens at the last level or at an escalation role that also passes its service level, whether the item then escalates to the committee level, holds, or raises an incident, and whether an escalated item may escalate again for ever. The deployment story also needs the refresh interval and the alert threshold, which are equally absent.
evidence: legacy section 3: "rwb.approval.route.D7.1.service-level=1 working day (assumed; DL22)" and "rwb.approval.service-level.default=3 working days (assumed ...; DL22)"; legacy AC2: "the approval moves to role RW-HEADLIT with escalation level 1 and a new due time of 09:00 on 16 December 2026"; R-UNI-30: "Raise the breach to the named escalation point. The case does not move"; TSD P7 T3.1 gives escalation_level as an integer with no ceiling.
owner_role: Business lead with the Center of excellence
proposed: Fix three values as data owned by RW-COE: the service level per decision and per default, the escalation step in working days, and a maximum escalation count with its ceiling behaviour (hold, incident to RW-RISK, or committee). Carry them as rwb.approval.service-level.*, rwb.approval.escalation.step and rwb.approval.escalation.max-levels and close DL22.

title: The data lake copy of the decision record is removed under DP-17 while the legacy log path streams to it
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37 (no data lake) and slides 28 and 44; TSD P7 v2 T5.1 (INT-19 and INT-20, daily batch); FSD P7 A2.6 (FEAT-DRI-06); plan DP-17; Template and Rules R6 (RWB-E1-014 retired)
description: The module specification keeps two daily outbound batches to a data lake and Power BI (INT-19) and to COLLINS through the lake (INT-20), and FEAT-DRI-06 streams decision entries to the lake for reporting, audit and model feedback. The target removes the data lake and reads reporting from events into rwb-reporting (DP-17, ADR-018), and RWB-E1-014, the decision-log copy job, is retired with no new story. The approval outcome of this key therefore has one delivery path, the DecisionRecorded event on rwb.decision-record.v1, and no lake partition, manifest or watermark, although the module specification still lists them.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 37 and DP-17: "Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 - Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting"; TSD P7 T5.1: "INT-19 Data lake and Power BI | Out | Daily batch | Daily"; Template and Rules R6 Retired: "RWB-E1-014 (decision log copy to the data lake: no data lake in Arch v5)".
proposed: State in the P7 stories, the event catalogue and TSD P7 next version that INT-19, INT-20, the lake partition, the manifest and the watermark are retired and that rwb-reporting builds its read model from rwb.decision-record.v1; keep EV-08 unchanged and drop every lake element from the contract and the deployment.

title: The request and answer field lists of the five approval operations and the case-status operation are not enumerated in any source
source: TSD P7 v2 appendix T-A.2 (ApprovalAction, ApprovalPage, ApprovalDetail and DecisionLogEntry named only) and T3.1; legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 4 and 12; Ownership Map v1 api section; FSD P7 A2.15 to A2.25
description: T-A.2 names a resource per operation and no property list: ApprovalAction is named without its fields, ApprovalDetail without its routing detail, ApprovalPage without page metadata, a default size or a maximum size, and DecisionLogEntry only as the answer of approve and refuse. The legacy story gives the business names of the action (reason, resolutionReference, reasonCode, changes, membersPresent) and the routing detail of the second read (regulationItem, limitVersion, ruleId, ruleVersion, dueAt, escalationLevel, sourceType, sourceRef, terms) but no types, lengths or optionality, and it leaves open whether a change above the caller's level is a 409 or a stored waiting item. The case status move of the flow (P3 moves the case from Waiting approval to In progress) has neither a named operation nor a named subscription in the Ownership Map, whose case surface carries no task-create and no case-status path.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 API-P7-003: "Request ApprovalAction | Response DecisionLogEntry" with no schema; TSD P7 T-A.2 API-P7-002: "Response ApprovalPage" with no page fields; legacy section 12: "Request ApprovalAction: reason, resolutionReference; added in this story: reasonCode (LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON), changes (the changed terms), membersPresent"; Ownership Map v1 api lists GET /cases/{caseId}, PATCH /tasks/{taskId} and GET /me/tasks but no task-create or case-status operation.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-013 (sections 4 steps 4 and 8, 11 DF-DEC-032 to DF-DEC-053, 12 and 13)
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-decision with the Solution architect
proposed: Baseline the five resources in RWB-P7-E2013-CON from the TSD P7 T3.1 field names in camelCase plus the platform page and error conventions, fix the required property of each ApprovalAction call, and add the case-status operation or the event subscription it maps to in the Ownership Map; the app story and the harness then build against one document.

title: The delegation snapshot and its cache refresh have no named operation, store or interval
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 41 and 42 (rwb.access.events.v1 DoaLimitChanged, consumers "all (cache refresh)"); Ownership Map v1 (delegation_limit owner P4); legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 3 and 13
description: The routing must read the version in force at the moment of the decision and the open approval must keep the version already stamped on it, so the service needs a warm snapshot of the delegation version and a refresh when the version changes. The target publishes DoaLimitChanged and gives its consumer as "all (cache refresh)", but no source names the refresh operation, the store of the snapshot, its interval or its owner, so the deployment cannot declare a warm-up step, a readiness gate, a Schedule or an alert on the age of the snapshot, and the app story cannot prove AC3 across a version change without choosing one.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 event table: "+ | AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged | rwb-access | rwb.access.events.v1 | all (cache refresh)"; arch v5 slide 14 P4 OUT: "topic rwb.access.events.v1: AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged"; legacy section 3 gives no refresh rule and section 13 lists no cache setting.
proposed: Fix one rule: the service holds the delegation version in a local read-through cache warmed at start before readiness and refreshed on DoaLimitChanged, with the effective date as the switch, no copied table and an alert when the cached version is older than the version in force; record the rule in RWB-P4-E1037-CON and in RWB-P7-E2013-OPS.

title: ApprovalDecided is named on the service contract slide but has no event catalogue row
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (rwb-decision OUT: ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce) against slide 42 rows 08, 09 and 30; TSD P7 v2 T5.3; legacy RWB-E2-013 section 12
description: The service contract slide gives rwb-decision three event types on rwb.decision.events.v1, ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided and RulePackageInForce, while the event catalogue carries only two of them: row 09 ApprovalRequested and row 30 RulePackageInForce, with row 08 DecisionRecorded on the shared topic. ApprovalDecided has no row, no event number and no consumer, and the legacy story publishes only EV-09 ApprovalRequested and EV-08 DecisionRecorded, so a baseline that declared ApprovalDecided would fix an event no catalogue, test or consumer owns.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14: "EVT rwb.decision.events.v1: ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce"; arch v5 slide 42 row 09: "| 09 | ApprovalRequested | rwb-decision | rwb.decision.events.v1 | gateway-bff (inbox) |" and row 30 RulePackageInForce, with no ApprovalDecided row; TSD P7 T5.3 lists DecisionRecorded and ApprovalRequested only.
proposed: Either add ApprovalDecided to the event catalogue with a number and its consumers, or delete it from slide 14 and rely on DecisionRecorded as the outcome event; until then no P7 story publishes it and the baseline records the absence.

title: The field-level list and the mask flags of the D7.1 approval screen are published by no source
source: RWB-E2-014 sections 4, 10 and 15; RWB-PLT-N001-CON 12.1
description: The legacy story names the facts on SCR-11 and SCR-18 (notice PDF, case number, product, total balance with its business date, addressee role, masked postal address, rule ID and version, template code and version, preparer) but no source enumerates the screen model's fields, their owners or their mask flags, and the gateway-bff route contract publishes seven routes, none of which is the approval screen.
evidence: RWB-E2-014 section 4 step 4 and AC10 name the facts as prose; RWB-PLT-N001-CON 12.1 lists GET /api/recovery/cases/{caseId}, /cases/{caseId}/documents, /notices, /payments, /legal-actions, /me/tasks and /inbox/stream only; the FSD P7 Screens table gives one line per screen.
proposed: Publish the field list and the mask flags of the two panels in RWB-P7-E2014-CON as the working read, and confirm them with the route owner and the three consumer sign-offs; correct by a new contract version.

title: The composite-route name and path segment of the approval screen are not specified
source: RWB-E2-014 sections 4 and 15; RWB-PLT-N001-CON 12.1; Architecture v5 slide 10
section: 7 Acceptance criteria AC1; 12.1; 15 Screens and states
description: The legacy story addresses the screen by the SCR-11 and SCR-18 identifiers and never names a route, and the platform route contract publishes a public base of /api/recovery with no service segment and no /v1 but no route for the approval screen.
evidence: RWB-E2-014 section 4 names GET /approvals/{approvalId} and GET /notices/{noticeId} as owner operations and no screen path; RWB-PLT-N001-CON AC1 enumerates the seven public routes it publishes.
proposed: Carry GET /api/recovery/approvals/{approvalId} as the working read in RWB-P7-E2014-CON and register it with the route owner at the first version freeze.

title: The limit that applies on the approval screen conflicts with D7.1 carrying no amount limit
source: REQ-APD-002; RWB-E2-014 sections 10 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41
description: REQ-APD-002 requires the approver to see on one screen the recommendation, the reasons, the inputs used and the limit that applies, while the legacy story states that a D7.1 notice carries no amount limit and delegation item 2.1.3 does not apply, and the DoA table itself is P4 rwb-access' and is not read for this decision.
evidence: REQ-APD-002 text in the Program BRD 5.7 and the Epic 2 BRD 3.7; RWB-E2-014 section 10 row 'Approval level | None'; Architecture v5 slide 14 (rwb-decision OUT: REST Access: DoA limits) and slide 41 (P4 owns the DoA table).
proposed: Show the approval level and the route role as the limit that applies for D7.1 (no amount, level none) and read the DoA table only where an amount-bearing decision uses the screen; confirm with Risk and Credit.

title: The module specification keeps two daily data-lake interfaces that DP-17 removes
source: TSD P7 v2 T5.1; REQ-DRI-009; DP-17; ADR-018; Architecture v5 slide 37
description: TSD P7 T5.1 still lists INT-19 (data lake and Power BI, out, daily batch) and INT-20 (COLLINS, out, daily batch to the data lake), and REQ-DRI-009 keeps a daily decision-log copy, while the target has no data lake, reporting reads events into rwb-reporting and JOB-13 becomes continuous Kafka ingest.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T5.1 table rows INT-19 and INT-20; Program BRD v4 REQ-DRI-009; Architecture v5 slide 37 and slide 44 JOB-13; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-17.
owner_role: Data steward and data product owner
proposed: Retire INT-19, INT-20 and the daily copy from the P7 documents in the next module-specification version; no lake element appears in this key's stories, chart or run book.

title: ApprovalDecided is named on the slide 14 contract line but has no event-catalogue row
source: Architecture v5 slide 14; slides 42 and 43
description: The rwb-decision OUT line of slide 14 names ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided and RulePackageInForce on rwb.decision.events.v1, while the event catalogue carries ApprovalRequested (09) and RulePackageInForce (30) and no ApprovalDecided; the decision outcome therefore leaves as the shared DecisionRecorded record.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 'EVT rwb.decision.events.v1: ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce' and slide 41 'topic rwb.decision.events.v1: ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce'; slides 42 and 43 row 09 and row 30 only.
proposed: Publish the decided outcome on rwb.decision-record.v1 through the local library (DP-03) and either retire ApprovalDecided from the slide 14 line or add it to the catalogue with its consumers.

title: REQ-APD-002 and REQ-APD-006 are mapped to two different features and stories
source: FSD P7 v3 A2.22; TSD P7 v2 T8
description: The FSD maps REQ-APD-002 and REQ-APD-006 to FEAT-APD-08 with RWB-E2-014, while the TSD traceability table maps both to FEAT-APD-01 with RWB-E2-013, the routing story.
evidence: FSD P7 v3 A1.2 (FEAT-APD-08 Approve demand and recall notices) and A2.22 acceptance rows naming RWB-E2-014; TSD P7 v2 T8 rows for REQ-APD-002 and REQ-APD-006 naming FEAT-APD-01 and RWB-E2-013.
proposed: Keep FEAT-APD-08 with RWB-E2-014 for the screen and FEAT-APD-01 with RWB-E2-013 for the routing, and correct the TSD traceability table in its next version.

title: The three notice operations of the legacy NoticeApi have no owner path
source: RWB-E2-014 section 12 (published interface NoticeApi); Ownership Map v1; RWB-P6-E1052-CON
description: The legacy story calls NoticeApi.approve, NoticeApi.regenerate and NoticeApi.hold on a notice, and the Ownership Map and the rwb-comms contract name no such operations, so AC1, AC2 and AC3 depend on an operation that has no published owner path.
evidence: RWB-E2-014 section 12 Java fragment with approve(UUID, UUID), regenerate(UUID, String) and hold(UUID, String, UUID); Ownership Map api names only POST /cases/{caseId}/notices, GET /notices/{noticeId} and POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve (owner S4); RWB-P6-E1052-CON 12.1 declares two operations.
proposed: Publish the notice decision operations on the rwb-comms contract (approve, regenerate, hold) with their states and error codes, or state that a notice is decided by one operation with an outcome code, and correct the Ownership Map rows.

title: Two consumed contracts carry no C row in this key
source: Ownership Map v1; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 45 (ADR-010)
description: The screen reads the total balance and the masked postal address through the rwb-source-data data-product contract and reads the case number and raises the case-owner task on the rwb-case contract, and this key's contract dependencies list neither, so the stories consume them against their fakes and the register has no dependency row.
evidence: WP B-P7-01 contract dependencies for RWB-P7-E2014-APP: RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-P6-E1052-CON; Architecture v5 slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the recovery.v_ace_* views); RWB-E2-014 section 11 names the P1 data-product interface and the P3 interface.
proposed: Add RWB-P1-E1015-CON and RWB-P3-E1018-CON as C rows of this key, or record the two reads as route-level composites of RWB-PLT-N001-CON; consume them against their fakes until the register closes the point.

title: The field types and order of the screen model and the queue paging defaults are not specified
source: TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 (API-P7-002); RWB-E2-014 sections 4 and 15
description: The module specification names the query parameters decision, product, page and size but no default, maximum or page shape beyond a page of approvals, and neither source fixes the data type or the order of the screen model's fields.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 API-P7-002 (Request: Query: decision, product, page, size; Response: ApprovalPage); RWB-E2-014 section 4 and AC10 name the fields as prose with no type.
proposed: Fix the page size default at 20 and the maximum at 100 and publish the field types in RWB-P7-E2014-CON; confirm with the front end and the route owner.

title: The legacy screen states and the platform route states are two unreconciled vocabularies
source: RWB-E2-014 section 15; RWB-PLT-N001-CON 15 and AC3
section: 7 Acceptance criteria AC4; 15 Screens and states
description: The legacy story declares Ready, Stale input and Decided for SCR-11 and Generated and Approved for the SCR-18 panel, while the platform route contract declares loading, loaded, temporarily unavailable and session expired at the edge; no source states how the two vocabularies combine on one screen.
evidence: RWB-E2-014 section 15 rows for SCR-11 and SCR-18; RWB-PLT-N001-CON section 15 and AC3 (four route states per area).
proposed: Keep READY, STALE_INPUT, DECIDED and GENERATED, APPROVED, HELD as the panel states and treat loading, temporarily unavailable and session expired as the route's own overlay states, as RWB-P7-E2014-CON AC4 states.

title: The notice summary excludes the PDF body and the addressee that the legacy screen shows
source: RWB-E2-014 AC10 and section 15; RWB-P6-E1052-CON BR8 and AC2
section: 7 Acceptance criteria AC5; 15 Screens and states
description: Legacy AC10 requires the screen to show the notice PDF, the addressee role and the postal address masked per the masking rules, while the notice answer of rwb-comms carries identifiers, codes, dates and a document ID only, with no notice body, no addressee and no account number.
evidence: RWB-E2-014 AC10 text; RWB-P6-E1052-CON AC2 ('carries no notice body, no addressee, no account number, no merge value and no name') and BR8.
proposed: Serve the PDF as the document reference of the notice answer through rwb-document at the route, and take the addressee role and the masked address from the rwb-source-data fields of the decision panel, as AC5 states.

title: No source enumerates the mask flags of the screen fields
source: Architecture v5 slide 35; RWB-E2-014 sections 4 and 15; RWB-PLT-N001-CON AC3
description: The legacy story says the postal address is masked per the masking rules and the platform route applies masking with the policy of rwb-access, but no source lists which screen field carries which mask flag or which policy key, and the masking table itself is P4 rwb-access'.
evidence: RWB-E2-014 section 4 step 4 ('postal address masked per the masking rules'); Architecture v5 slide 35 (masking by policy); Ownership Map tables masking_rule owner P4; RWB-PLT-N001-CON AC3 (coarse permission, object-level authorisation with the owner).
proposed: Declare a mask flag of NONE, PARTIAL or FULL with a policy key on every field of the two panels, PARTIAL for the postal address, and confirm the policy keys with the masking owner (P4).

title: The timeout budget of a screen that composes three reads is not specified
source: RWB-PLT-N001-CON AC2 and AC4; Architecture v5 slide 10
description: The platform route publishes a 2 s timeout per downstream and a 1.2 s budget for the case screen only; no budget is stated for the approval screen, which composes the approval, the notice and the account facts, so the registration cannot inherit a published figure.
evidence: RWB-PLT-N001-CON AC2 (0.15 s gateway plus 0.6 s slowest parallel call plus 0.3 s merge, about 1.2 s) and AC4 (2 s per downstream); Architecture v5 slide 10 (one hop, 2 s).
proposed: Register the route with a 2 s budget per downstream and the same 1.2 s composition budget as the case screen, and record the measured p95 on the dashboard.

title: The dashboard names, the alert thresholds and the empty-queue window are not specified
source: ADR-023; Architecture v5 slides 20 and 44; REQ-APD-006
description: ADR-023 requires observability per service and the legacy story gives a service level of 1 working day, but no source names the dashboard, the alert thresholds of the approval screen or the window after which an empty D7.1 queue is an incident.
evidence: ADR-023 (observability per service); RWB-E2-014 section 3 (1 working day service level) and section 2 (measure: notices sent with an approval entry, 100 percent); no threshold in the FSD P7 or TSD P7 observability text.
proposed: Alert on any 5xx in five minutes, on a route p95 above the registered budget, on a failed record write and on an empty D7.1 queue for 24 hours, and review the thresholds with the platform observability owner.
